name: AX Feishu Bridge
summary: Bridges Pi conversations into Feishu and Lark bots.
recommendation: Use it when you need chat access from Feishu/Lark and can review the bot credential setup first.
notes: Handles bot credentials and outbound messaging; review the setup docs before enabling it in a workspace.

name: Pi LSP
summary: Exposes configurable LSP tooling through a shared Pi extension.
recommendation: Use it when you want language-server diagnostics and code actions without tying Pi to one language.
notes: The public source lives in a monorepo under packages/pi-lsp.

name: Pi Memory
summary: Adds persistent long-term memory, daily logs, a scratchpad, and optional semantic search to Pi.
recommendation: Use it when decisions and context must survive sessions and local Markdown storage fits your workflow.
notes: Semantic and deep search optionally invoke qmd and local embedding workflows.

name: Pi Powerline Footer
summary: Adds a powerline-style status footer to Pi.
recommendation: Use it when you want a denser TUI status bar and your Pi version matches the published peer range.
notes: The published peer dependency range targets Pi 0.81.x through 0.84.x.

name: Pi Subagents
summary: Adds delegation and scripted multi-agent workflows to Pi.
recommendation: Use it when you need repeatable task fanout and are ready to review the extra model and tool permissions it can invoke.
notes: Can launch background runs and additional agent sessions.

name: Pi Web Access
summary: Adds web search, page fetching, and content extraction tools to Pi.
recommendation: Use it when you need multi-provider web access and can audit the provider-specific credentials or browser-session features you enable.
notes: Some providers use API keys, cookies, or browser-session access; enable only the integrations you trust.

name: Ponytail
summary: Adds an always-on minimalism discipline and focused skills for reducing over-engineering.
recommendation: Use it when you want coding agents to prefer YAGNI, standard-library solutions, and deletion over speculative abstractions.
notes: Changes coding-agent behavior through an extension and skills rather than changing project runtime code.

name: Superpowers
summary: Adds a structured software-development methodology built from composable agent skills.
recommendation: Use it when you want explicit brainstorming, TDD, debugging, planning, review, and worktree workflows.
notes: Its behavioral skills add approval gates and process requirements to coding tasks.
